query:
Which supplied authorities help analyze the live Delhi DRC1958s14(1)(b) issue shown by this allowed record, respecting the target procedural stage, rival assertions and scope limits? Do not predict the withheld target verdict.
Facts of the case in brief are as under that:-
Petitioner has filed this petition for eviction of tenant/respondent under cite8†Section 14 (1) (b) of DRC Act on the ground of "subletting"
CASE No. RC - 01/08 2/10 by the respondent. The facts alleged by the petitioner are as under that he is the owner of the property bearing number H. No. 455, Wazirpur, Delhi. Respondent no. 1 is his tenant under the petitioner in respect of one shop shown as red colour in the site plan on a monthly rent of Rs. 300/- excluding of other charges. Respondent no.
1 has illegally and without the consent in writing of the petitioner/ owner/ landlord has sublet, assigned and part with the tenanted shop with respondent no. 2 and has shifted himself in Bahadrabad, Distt. Haridwar, Uttrakhand. Respondent no. 2 is a legal tenant and is in exclusive possession and in full control of the tenanted shop and he is running the business in the said shop himself exclusively. One notice dated 12.08.2008 was sent to the responsible no. 1. The tenancy of respondent no.
1 is expired on 30.11.2008 cite9†u/s. 106 of Transfer of Property Act. Thus, this petition.
2. In his Written Statement, the respondent has stated that respondent no. 1 has not illegally subleted the shop to respondent no. 2. Respondent no.1 is running a printing press in the said premises till today in the name and style of S.R. Printer and respondent no. 1 is the sole proprietor of the said shop. Respondent no. 2 is the son of respondent no. 1, who is only assisting the respondent no. 1 for conducting the business activities. Respondent no.
1 is a devotee Hindu and pay visit to Haridwar and other holy places occasionally and respondent no. 2 is assisting in conducting his business.
3. It is important to mention here that petitioner has examined only one witness i.e., petitioner himself and respondent has examined two witness i.e., respondent no. 1 & 2 themselves.
4. Petitioner in his evidence has stated that he is the owner of the suit property bearing number 455, Wazirpur, Delhi and respondent no. 1, is the tenant in this shop. The site plan is Ex. PW1/1. He is the old tenant in the said shop. The CASE No. RC - 01/08 3/10 copy of the counter rent receipt dated 01.09.2002 is Ex. PW1/1. The respondent no.
1 illegally and without the consent of the petitioner, who is landlord, has subletting, assign or part with the shop to Sanjeev Kumar after June, 1952 and has shifted himself Bahadrabad, Distt. Haridwar, Uttrakhand permanently. Respondent no. 2 is in exclusive possession and in full control in the tenanted shop and he is running the business in the said shop himself exclusively and opens and closes the shop himself. A notice dated 12.08.2008 was sent to respondent no. 1 which was duly received by him.
Copy of the notice Ex. PW1/3. Postal receipt is Ex. PW1/4 and acknowledgment card is Ex. PW1/5. Respondent no. 2 have not replied to this legal notice. In his cross examination petitioner has stated that at present son of respondent no. 1 is carrying on the business, however, the board of S.R. Printer is still there. During cross examination, petitioner has further stated that tenanted premises is still being used for printing work, till today since the inception of tenancy.
5. Respondent no. 1, on the other hand, has stated in his evidence that he is running the printing press in house number 455, Wazirpur, Delhi, in the name and style of S.R. Printer and he is the sole proprietor of the said concern. It is further stated that respondent no. 2 is his son, who is only assisting him in conducting the business activities since respondent no.
1 has settled the business with the passage of time so he is not able to look after of the business activities which has diversified in many fields. Respondent no. 1 is in full control of his business as well as tenanted premises. It is further stated by the respondent no.1 that he has given the reply to the notice given by the petitioner.
6. During his cross examination, it is stated by the respondent, Shyam Singh, that Sanjeev Kumar, his son, opens and closes the shop and sits at the said shop in the capacity of his son. During cross examination, it is further stated by the respondent no. 1, Shyam Singh that Sanjeev Kumar is neither partner nor the CASE No. RC - 01/08 4/10 employee in the said shop. Submission with regard to the subletting or parting with said shop with the Sanjeev Kumar has been declined by the Shyam Singh.
Thus, during cross examination, it is stated by him that his son used to help him in his work due to his illness.
7. Sanjeev Kumar, respondent no. 2, on the other hand, has stated in his evidence that his father is running a printing press at shop no. 1 in H.No. 455, Wazirpur, Delhi in the name and style of S.R. Printer. His father is sole proprietor of the said concern. Sanjeev Kumar, respondent no.
2, being the son of Shyam Singh only assisting him in conducting the business activities since his father has settled the business with the passage of time and is not able to look after all the business activities which has been diversified in many fields. It is stated by respondent no. 2 that his father is in full control of this business.
8. During his cross examination, Sanjeev Kumar has corroborated in his examination in chief. He has stated that he is neither the partner nor the employee of the said firm. He is only assisting his father. It is further stated by him that he is living jointly with his father. It is further stated by him tha he is living jointly with his father.
9. After examining the witness brought by both the sides, parties have advanced their final arguments. During arguments petitioner has stated that respondent, Shyam Singh has part with the possession of the tenanted premises and has subletted the said premises to respondent no. 2, Sanjeev Kumar, who is his son. This fact is denied by the respondent and during arguments, it is stated by their counsel that allowing respondent no. 2 being the son of respondent no.
1 to look after the business only in the capacity of son of respondent no. 1 and it does not amounting to subletting.
